patterns_found.visual_evidence: Both sketches place a horizontal navigation/header bar at the very top of the page, visually separated from the content below and spanning the width like a persistent site header.
patterns_found.behavior_notes: Header should remain available while scrolling, especially because the page appears long and content-heavy. Active nav state is also implied by one emphasized nav item.
patterns_found.ambiguities: The sketches do not explicitly show the header during scrolled states, so fixed/sticky behavior is inferred from the persistent top-bar treatment rather than directly depicted.

patterns_found.visual_evidence: Each sketch shows a compact search control in the header area: on mobile a small square icon/button at the right of the top bar, and on desktop a boxed search field/button cluster beneath or within the nav area.
patterns_found.behavior_notes: Search should accept text and submit on button press or Enter. On mobile, the icon likely toggles or reveals the search field; on desktop, the search control appears directly available.
patterns_found.ambiguities: It is unclear whether mobile search expands inline, opens a hidden field, or navigates to a dedicated search page.

patterns_found.visual_evidence: The search UI in both sketches includes an input-like control paired with a trigger button, implying a submittable form.
patterns_found.behavior_notes: At minimum, the search field should validate basic input state before submit, manage empty submissions, and support keyboard submission.
patterns_found.ambiguities: The sketches do not indicate whether empty search is allowed or whether inline error messaging is expected.

patterns_found.visual_evidence: Interactive header controls include nav items plus search trigger/input combinations; on mobile especially, the compact top-bar search affordance implies a reveal/hide interaction that requires moving focus into the opened control.
patterns_found.behavior_notes: When search is expanded or revealed, focus should move into the input; when closed, focus should return to the trigger. Keyboard navigation across header controls should remain logical.
patterns_found.ambiguities: This depends on whether the mobile search is a disclosure, overlay, or inline expansion.

sketch_notes: The sketches imply a relatively low-JS page centered on content reading, with the main interactive complexity concentrated in the top header/search area rather than in the body content. Desktop appears to expose search more directly, while mobile compresses header actions and likely requires a reveal interaction for search. No clear evidence appears for hamburger navigation, dropdowns, tabs, accordions, modals, toasts, or progressive loading; most remaining elements read as static links, article text, and footer navigation.
